note: WHICH PAGES DECLARE WHAT THEY REST ON, AND WHICH DELIBERATELY DO NOT. Row 186 measured that 0 of this archive's pages declared their sources against Defranceski's 39, and the first instinct on fixing it was to put a block on all of them. THAT WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN NOTHING. A process page that lists documents is claiming to rest on evidence it does not use; an index page would carry the same list three hundred times whether it applied or not; and /sources/ would point every id at a row three inches below it. SO THE ABSENCE IS RECORDED AS A DECISION RATHER THAN LEFT AS A GAP, with a reason per page, and a gate refuses a page that is in neither list — because the state this row was really about is not 'undeclared', it is 'nobody has considered it'.

exempt.404.astro: A not-found page. It argues nothing and rests on nothing.
exempt.about.astro: About the archive itself — who made it and why. Its subject is the project, not the family.
exempt.method.astro: How this archive reasons. Its evidence is its own mistakes, which are at /corrections/, not in the source register.
exempt.changes.astro: A log of what changed here and when. It rests on this site's own history.
exempt.corrections.astro: Things published and taken back. Each row names the document that overturned it IN THE ROW, which is a better place than a block at the foot of the page.
exempt.errands.astro: What can only be got through a door. By definition these are documents NOT yet held, so a block of sources would list the one thing the page is about not having.
exempt.open-questions.astro: What is not known, with the record set that would answer each. Every row names its own target; a page-level block would name the documents this archive has, which are the ones that did NOT answer.
exempt.searched.astro: Every query ever run here. The row IS the citation — source, url, outcome — and a block above them would be a second, weaker statement of the same thing.
exempt.worklist.astro: Who is doing what. It rests on nothing but itself.
exempt.search.astro: A search box over this site's own index.
exempt.sources.astro: THE REGISTER ITSELF. A page cannot rest on itself, and a block here would point every id at the row three inches below it.
exempt.people.astro: An index of people, built from people.js. Each person's own page carries the documents; this one carries the list.
exempt.who.astro: An index of names, built from the register. The same reasoning as /people/.
exempt.who/index.astro: An index of names. The evidence is on the person pages it links to.
exempt.who/[slug].astro: One name at a time, generated. Each carries the documents for that person; a shared block would be the same list on three hundred pages whether or not it applied.
exempt.people/[slug].astro: One person at a time, generated. The documents are named in the person's own record, which is where a reader is looking.
exempt.places/index.astro: An index of places, built from places.json.
exempt.places/[slug].astro: One place at a time, generated. Each pin names the document that witnesses it, on the pin.
exempt.register.astro: The harvested FamilySearch register — 7,600 index rows this archive pulled itself. Its source is the harvest, which is named at the head of the page and is not one of the 46 documents.
exempt.trees.astro: A chooser for the drawn lines. The evidence is on /tree/, which declares.
exempt.bloodline.astro: A chart built around whichever person a reader picks. It rests on the whole register rather than on any part of it, and /tree/ carries the declaration for the drawn line.
exempt.atlas.astro: The map. Every pin on it already carries its own witness in places.json, and a gate refuses an unwitnessed pin — so the provenance is per-pin and finer than a page-level block.
exempt.dna.astro: Two DNA kits. Its evidence is a pair of test results and a shared-match list, which are not documents and are not in the source register. The one thing on this page that IS documentary is argued at /cousins/, which declares.
